item.title: Poor street work and cleanliness carried out by council, 10th August
item.description:
I am contacting you regarding the recent tarmac/pavement works carried out by the council or its contractor immediately outside my property. Unfortunately, the area has been left in a very poor condition following the works. A significant amount of dried concrete/cement residue and construction dirt has been left across the pavement and, more importantly, over my private block-paved driveway. Tarmac from the works has also been left between and against the blocks at the edge of my driveway. My driveway was not in this condition before the works were undertaken and I do not consider it reasonable for my private property to have been left covered in construction residue and tarmac as a result of council works. I have photographs taken immediately following the works which clearly show the condition in which the pavement and my driveway have been left. Please can you arrange for the works to be inspected and for the contractor to return to: 1. Remove the dried concrete/cement residue and construction dirt from my driveway. 2. Remove any tarmac that has been left on or between my block paving. 3. Properly reinstate the boundary between the pavement and my driveway without damaging the existing paving. 4. Clean the pavement and driveway and leave the area in an appropriate condition following the works. I would appreciate confirmation that this has been passed to the appropriate Highways officer/contractor and when I can expect the remedial work to be carried out. I have retained photographs of the condition of the area following the works.

Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): Inglewood Road, Barnehurst, Greater London

item.title: Severe property and safety hazard caused by an overgrown council tree. Overextended branches hang directly over my roof, driveway, and garden, presenting an imminent risk of structural damage and falling branch hazards. Furthermore, the branches extend over the public street and pavement, dropping heavy volumes of hard, walnut-like nuts. This debris creates a major obstruction and a severe slip/trip hazard that causes pain and personal injury to pedestrians walking on the pavement. Urgent cutting back is required., 10th August
item.description:
The council tree is heavily overgrown and unmaintained, creating an immediate danger to both my private property and the public highway.Specifically:Property Risk: Overextended branches hang directly over my roof, scraping tiles during high winds, and threaten to snap onto my driveway and garden.Public Safety Hazard: Branches hanging over the pavement drop large volumes of hard, walnut-like nuts. This creates a severe trip and slip hazard that causes physical pain and injury to pedestrians stepping on them.
Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): Gattons Way, North Cray, Greater London
